operator_casefile.project_type: Non-flight-authorizing 450 mm class quadcopter assembly and bench-validation concept using a documented Pixhawk 6C with PX4
functional_subsystems: Pixhawk 6C flight controller and PX4 configuration
Regulated flight-controller power subsystem with POWER1 and POWER2 supply paths
Power module, battery-side sensing, and controller-side power isolation
Four propulsion channels, each consisting of a motor, ESC, propeller, wiring, and mechanical mount
Battery, primary distribution, ESC power wiring, connectors, fusing or protection as required by the final electrical design
PWM ESC signal and ground interface from Pixhawk 6C outputs
450 mm-class frame, landing structure, motor mounts, vibration management, and payload attachment provisions
Ground-side configuration and bench-only test equipment
Documentation package containing wiring, BOM, calculations, configuration records, and unresolved assumptions

decision_tree.next_action: Reject any catalog build that is not an aerial multirotor or that lacks four motor/ESC channels, a compatible frame, and a documented Pixhawk 6C interface.
decision_tree.purpose: Prevent an irrelevant demo build from being treated as the requested quadcopter assembly.

decision_tree.next_action: Retain the bench_power_adapter recommendation only as a bench-validation accessory; do not treat it as the aircraft battery, propulsion power source, or complete assembly.
decision_tree.purpose: Use the catalog item only where it supports the explicitly bench-only scope.

decision_tree.next_action: Obtain the exact Pixhawk 6C power-module model and its input, output, current, connector, sensing, and isolation specifications.
decision_tree.purpose: Design POWER1 and POWER2 correctly without connecting the battery directly to a regulated POWER port.

decision_tree.next_action: Select or document four compatible motor, ESC, propeller, battery, and power-distribution combinations only after voltage, current, connector, mounting, and firmware-interface compatibility are verified.
decision_tree.purpose: Avoid assumed thrust, runtime, current, or replacement-part compatibility.

decision_tree.next_action: Collect motor thrust-current data for the exact motor, propeller, battery voltage, and ESC operating conditions.
decision_tree.purpose: Complete the thrust-to-weight, expected-current, battery-sizing, and thermal calculations.

decision_tree.next_action: Resolve the four rotor actuator source-part bindings and provide measured or designed joint limits for front-left, front-right, rear-right, and rear-left rotor joints.
decision_tree.purpose: Close the structured topology gaps before assembly documentation is considered complete.

decision_tree.next_action: Define the frame geometry, motor spacing, total mass budget, payload, center of gravity, and mechanical envelope.
decision_tree.purpose: Verify the 450 mm classification, dimensional fit, stability, and payload margin.

decision_tree.next_action: Create a bench-only PX4 configuration and validation procedure with propellers removed and no flight authorization.
decision_tree.purpose: Validate interfaces and configuration without authorizing operation in flight.

compatible_parts_or_requirements: The documented source claims state that Pixhawk 6C POWER1 and POWER2 require regulated supply through a suitable power module.
The battery must not be wired directly to a regulated Pixhawk 6C POWER port.
The documented source claims state that Pixhawk 6C supports PWM servo outputs and PX4 multicopter configurations.
The documented source claims state that Pixhawk 6C supports power-module, GPS/compass, and ESC-interface wiring.
A power module must provide a verified regulated controller output and compatible voltage, current, connector, pinout, sensing, and isolation characteristics; the exact model is unknown.
Four ESCs must be compatible with the selected battery voltage, motor current envelope, cooling conditions, signal interface, connector scheme, and PX4 output assignment; exact ESCs are unknown.

Four motors must have verified mounting dimensions, shaft or propeller interface, voltage range, KV, continuous and peak current data, and thrust tables for the selected propellers; exact motors are unknown.
Propellers must be selected only from verified motor, battery-voltage, rotation-direction, clearance, and thrust-current data; propeller size and type are unknown.
The battery must have verified nominal voltage, capacity, continuous discharge capability, peak capability, connector, physical dimensions, and mass; battery voltage and capacity are unknown.
The frame and motor mounts must provide verified 450 mm-class geometry, structural compatibility, clearance, and landing support; measured dimensions and mechanical evidence are missing.
The catalog recommendation bench_power_adapter is potentially compatible with the bench-only scope, but its electrical ratings and compatibility with the planned power path are unverified.
build_or_repair_sequence: Freeze the non-flight scope and label the aircraft as not flight-authorized.
Document the Pixhawk 6C connector pinouts and PX4 output mapping from the cited documentation, then obtain the exact hardware revision and connector implementation.
Define the battery-side distribution path, power-module input path, regulated controller output, POWER1/POWER2 allocation, sensing path, grounds, protection, and isolation boundaries.
Create a four-channel propulsion interface table covering motor, ESC, battery, propeller, connector, PWM signal, signal ground, power conductors, and mechanical mounting.

Collect exact motor-propeller-battery thrust and current data, then calculate total thrust, thrust-to-weight ratio, hover and peak current, battery energy, voltage sag margin, ESC margin, conductor sizing, and expected runtime.
Define frame geometry, rotor orientation, motor locations, clearance, landing structure, center of gravity, payload allowance, and vibration-control provisions.
Bind each front-left, front-right, rear-right, and rear-left actuator role to a declared structured part and document designed or measured joint limits.
Produce the assembly wiring diagram, power-rail diagram, connector and polarity schedule, BOM, mass budget, and unresolved-assumption register.
Configure PX4 for the documented Pixhawk 6C, frame type, output mapping, sensor interfaces, safety settings, and calibration requirements without enabling flight authorization.

Perform only bench validation with propellers removed: continuity and polarity checks, isolated rail checks, regulated-output checks, controller boot and power redundancy checks, sensor recognition, GPS/compass interface checks, ESC signal checks without propulsion operation, logging, and fault recording.
Update the design only after measured or documented evidence resolves the electrical, propulsion, mechanical, thermal, and topology unknowns.
critical_technical_unknowns: Exact Pixhawk 6C hardware revision, connector pinout, and required POWER1/POWER2 operating ranges
Power module model, regulated output ratings, input range, current-sensing range, voltage-sensing range, connector pinout, and isolation behavior
Battery nominal voltage, maximum voltage, capacity, discharge rating, connector, dimensions, and mass
Motor model, KV, winding or phase characteristics, mounting pattern, voltage range, continuous current, peak current, and thrust data
Propeller manufacturer, diameter, pitch, material, rotation direction, clearance, and thrust-current data
ESC models, voltage/current ratings, cooling, firmware, input signal compatibility, telemetry capability, BEC behavior, connectors, and peak margin
Frame mass, arm length, rotor spacing, motor-mount pattern, structural limits, vibration behavior, and actual 450 mm classification
Total empty mass, payload mass, maximum takeoff mass, center of gravity, and required thrust-to-weight margin
Expected hover and peak current, battery voltage sag, energy consumption, thermal loads, and runtime target
Power-distribution-board or harness ratings, conductor gauge, connector ratings, protection strategy, and grounding topology
GPS/compass model, mounting location, cable compatibility, interference-control requirements, and availability
PX4 release, parameter set, output assignment, sensor calibration state, safety configuration, and documented controller firmware compatibility
Rotor actuator source-part identifiers for all four topology slots
Designed or measured joint limits for all four rotor joints
Runtime target, budget limit, measured dimensions, mechanical simulation, bench evidence, reviewed release scope, and payload limits
Inputs for runtime analysis: battery energy or voltage and capacity plus continuous or average load power
Inputs for current-margin analysis: supply-current limit, peak current, and per-load peak or stall current
Inputs for payload-margin analysis: payload mass and payload limit
Inputs for static-stability analysis: support width or wheel track and combined center-of-gravity height
Inputs for actuator-torque analysis: payload mass, payload lever arm, and actuator continuous torque
Inputs for dimensional-envelope analysis: candidate width and maximum width
Inputs for thermal analysis: estimated power loss, thermal resistance, ambient temperature, and maximum component temperature
validation_plan: Review all source claims against the cited PX4 Pixhawk 6C and wiring documentation; treat them as documentation claims, not physical test results.
Verify the final wiring diagram prevents direct battery connection to any regulated Pixhawk 6C POWER port.
Verify the selected power module's regulated outputs, sensing, current limits, connector pinout, and isolation against its manufacturer documentation before use.
Check the battery-side wiring, connector polarity, conductor ratings, protection, and distribution ratings against calculated continuous and peak currents.
Recalculate total mass, thrust-to-weight ratio, hover current, peak current, battery energy, voltage sag margin, and runtime only from exact motor-propeller-battery evidence.
Verify each ESC-to-motor pairing, ESC signal path, signal ground, output assignment, rotation direction, and fault behavior without installed propellers.
Verify frame clearances, motor mounting, rotor geometry, center of gravity, payload envelope, and all four topology bindings from design or measurement evidence.
Perform controller power-up, rail, redundancy, sensor, GPS/compass, and logging checks on the bench only.
Perform PX4 configuration and calibration checks with propulsion disabled and propellers removed.
Record every unresolved discrepancy, failed check, and missing source document; do not authorize flight from this protocol.
Use a second-person or independent review of the power-rail design, propulsion calculations, wiring, BOM, and PX4 parameter set before any scope change.
